rubric_items.deep_module: pass — the change is one module-private function over the nodes `definitions` already yields, hiding the whole rule (the callee set incl. bare `replace`/`rename`, the local-binding decidability test, the parameter-rename one-level-up resolution, the module-level-name move exclusion) behind a single node-inventory interface; it adds no parallel walker.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: pass — the one re-derivation, porting the census staged-write predicate into reckon/interface_counts.py, is justified and reconciled rather than forked: the census imports its sibling `candidates` unqualified at module scope (census.py:24) so a package caller cannot import it, its figures are compared across pinned commits so its predicate is frozen, and §9 binds the runtime owner to it with a one-directional parity assertion (census ⊆ runtime, the correct direction since the runtime rule is strictly broader); the frames, scheduler queries and state readers it touches are routed to their owners, not duplicated.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1475, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §9 names its accounting in its own text — the inventory rule is module-private (definitions' publicity rule at interface_counts.py:88 excludes `_`-prefixed names) and the deleted helpers were private and uncounted, so public_definitions does not grow and nothing is retired; the section adds no CLI option, MCP view or refusal family, and its done-when pins the claim ("public_definitions no higher than at the base").
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — §9 cites and extends existing machinery rather than adding a subsystem: the AST walker `read_trees`/`definitions` (reckon/interface_counts.py:326, :76), the staged-write predicate lifted from the census `primitive_concepts` (docs/research/data/crew-pattern-review/code-depth/census.py:233-274), and the §8 owner `write_atomically` (reckon/_store.py:426); its write-site inventory is accurate (serve.py's four sites at :498, :562, :2322, :3629; ledger.py's two at :1032 and :1168; archive.py:137; evidence.py:676), and the two sites it names as retained exceptions genuinely cannot reach the file-writing primitive.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — §9 adds no layer: it deletes the private temporary-and-rename helper around each site and renders through the §8 owner (§9's `binary=True` reuses the keyword `_store.write_atomically` already carries), so the honest extension of the existing mechanism is what the plan does.
